problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨2{e}^{2t},\,3{t}^{2}+2t⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨1,2⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=1.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Displacement Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $r=⟨0,0⟩$ when $t=3,$ calculate the position of $P$ at time $t=\frac{1}{2}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t),\,\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 2\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)\,\text{d}t,\int \pi \operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(3)=⟨0,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(3) & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\pi )+{C}_{1},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨2+{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=-2$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the position vector at time $t$ is given by

$$
r(t)=⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi t)-2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi t)⟩.
$$

To find the position vector at time $t=\frac{1}{2},$ we substitute $t=\frac{1}{2}$ into the above, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{1}{2}) & =⟨-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi \cdot \frac{1}{2})-2,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi \cdot \frac{1}{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0-2,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
